merger_name: INPEX – Further interest in the Ichthys LNG Project
merger_description:
INPEX Corporation (**INPEX**) is an oil and gas exploration and production company headquartered in Tokyo, Japan. Its main business includes research, exploration, development, production and sales of oil, natural gas and other mineral resources.

A subsidiary of INPEX operates the Ichthys LNG Project, and INPEX subsidiaries have a 67.82% interest in the Ichthys LNG Project.

Ichthys LNG Pty Ltd is an incorporated joint venture holding certain assets for the Ichthys LNG Project. Ichthys LNG Pty Ltd owns the gas export pipeline, onshore LNG plant and storage and offloading facilities for the Ichthys LNG Project and conducts marketing activities on behalf of the joint venture. The upstream assets for the Ichthys LNG Project are owned by an unincorporated joint venture.

The Ichthys LNG Project produces up to 9.3 million tonnes of LNG per annum at peak, as well as Liquified Petroleum Gas (**LPG**) and condensate as by-products. The Ichthys LNG Project operates across the chain of development and production of LNG, including subsea, offshore, pipeline and onshore LNG. Gas and condensate from the Ichthys gas field is exported to onshore facilities for processing near Darwin via an 890-kilometre pipeline. Almost all gas and condensate produced is exported overseas.

In addition to its interest in the Ichthys LNG Project, INPEX indirectly holds minority participating interests in other floating liquefied natural gas (**FLNG**), liquified natural gas (**LNG**) and oil field projects in Australia and interests in leases relating to oil and gas exploration.

JERA is a Japanese energy company involved in upstream development, fuel procurement and power generation, and wholesale supply of electricity and gas.

The Acquisition principally comprises:

* INPEX Ichthys acquiring JERA’s 0.735% interest in the unincorporated Ichthys joint venture, which owns certain Commonwealth petroleum retention leases and titles, upstream infrastructure such as the floating production, storage and offloading facility and the central processing facility plus the rights, title and interests in certain asset documents regarding the Ichthys LNG Project, and
* INPEX Holdings acquiring JERA’s 0.735% interest in Ichthys LNG Pty Ltd

(together, the **Target Assets**).

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. INPEX (through its wholly owned INPEX subsidiaries)
already owns a majority interest in the Ichthys LNG Project
b. the Acquisition would lead to a very small increase in
INPEX’s share of the production and supply of natural gas,
the wholesale supply of LNG, and the production and supply
of LPG and condensate in Australia and globally (to the
extent it is already produced from the Ichthys LNG Project)
c. there are alternative producers and suppliers in the
exploration of crude oil and natural gas, the production and
supply of natural gas, the wholesale supply of LNG, and the
production and supply of LPG and condensate in Australia
and globally.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
